items.title: 6.1 Gases ke kinetic theory ke mafrooze (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 6.1 with Figs. 6.1 to 6.3, Example 6.1 and thermal equilibrium (PDF 119-124).

blocks.text: Thermodynamics physics ki woh shakh (branch) hai jo heat (garmi) aur energy ki doosri shaklon ke darmiyan rishte aur ek se doosri mein badalne ko parhti hai. Is mein bari scale (macroscopic) par systems ke rawaiye ke usool aate hain, jaise temperature, pressure (dabao) aur volume. Isi liye thermodynamics technology mein bohat aham hai, kyun ke hamare istemal ki taqreeban saari kachchi (raw) energy heat ki shakal mein hi nikalti hai. Is chapter mein hum gases ka rawaiya aur thermodynamics ke qawaneen (laws), un ki ahmiyat aur istemal parhenge.

Kinetic theory of gases physics aur chemistry ki ek bunyadi theory hai. Yeh gases ke rawaiye ko un ke chhote zarron (particles) ki harkat se samjhati hai, aur pressure, temperature aur volume jaisi gas ki khoobiyon ki bari scale par samajh deti hai. Is theory ke aham assumptions (farz ki gayi baatein) yeh hain:
1. Gas ke particles hamesha be-tarteeb (random) harkat mein hain
Gas ke molecules hamesha be-tarteeb harkat mein rehte hain. Woh seedhi lines mein chalte hain jab tak kisi doosre molecule ya bartan (container) ki deewar se takra na jayein.
2. Gas ke particles ka volume na hone ke barabar hai
Ek ek molecule ka volume gas ke kul volume ke muqable mein bohat hi kam (negligible) hai. Is liye particles ko aise point masses mana jata hai jin ka apna koi khaas volume nahi.
3. Molecules ke darmiyan koi force nahi
Gas ke molecules ek doosre ko na kheenchte hain (attraction) na dhakelte hain (repulsion). Takrane ke waqt ke siwa woh ek doosre par koi force nahi lagate.
4. Elastic collisions (takkarein)
Molecules ki aapas mein aur deewaron se takkarein poori tarah elastic hain, yani takkar mein kinetic energy bilkul zaya nahi hoti. Kul kinetic energy wahi rehti hai (conserved).
5. Particles ki bohat bari tadaad
Gas mein particles bohat zyada hote hain. Itni bari tadaad ki wajah se gas ki khoobiyan statistical methods (ausat aur hisab ke tareeqe) se bayan ki ja sakti hain.
6. Ausat kinetic energy temperature ke mutabiq hai

Gas ke particles ki ausat (average) kinetic energy gas ke absolute temperature (Kelvin temperature) ke seedha mutabiq (directly proportional) hai. Yani temperature barhe to particles ki speed bhi barhti hai.
7. Pressure particles ki takkaron se banta hai
Gas bartan ki deewaron par jo pressure dalti hai woh particles ke deewaron se takrane ki wajah se hai. Takkar ke waqt particles jo force lagate hain wahi pressure banati hai.
8. Takkar ka waqt na hone ke barabar hai
Do particles ki takkar bohat hi thore waqt mein ho jati hai, do takkaron ke darmiyan ke waqt ke muqable mein. Is farz se particles ki harkat ka hisab aasaan ho jata hai.
Kinetic molecular theory ki hadein (limitations)
Real gases

Kinetic theory ke assumptions ideal gases par poore utarte hain. Real gases in se hat jati hain (deviation), kyun ke un ke molecules ke darmiyan forces hoti hain aur molecules ka apna volume bhi hota hai; yeh farq khaas taur par high pressure aur low temperature par nazar aata hai.

Mukhtasar yeh ke kinetic theory gas ke rawaiye ki bari tasveer deti hai: pressure aur temperature jaisi naapi jane wali cheezon ko gas particles ki harkat se jorti hai, aur thermodynamics aur statistical mechanics samajhne ki bunyad hai.
Ideal gas ki equation of state
Jo gas kinetic theory ke mutabiq chale use ideal gas kehte hain. Ideal gas ki equation (muadla) yeh hai:
Yahan P pressure, V volume, n gas ke moles ki tadaad, R universal gas constant (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) aur T temperature hai.
Equation (6.1) batati hai ke ideal gas ke liye pressure aur volume ka hasil-e-zarb (product) temperature ke seedha mutabiq hai.
Real gas kab ideal gas jaisi ho jati hai

Kinetic theory ke mutabiq gas ke molecules ke darmiyan koi kheench-taan (interaction) nahi aur woh ek doosre se door hote hain. Real gas ideal gas jaisi tab hogi jab kuch shartein poori hon: molecules ki P.E. (potential energy) na hone ke barabar ho aur un ke paas sirf K.E. (kinetic energy) ho.
Eq. (6.1) mein n moles ki tadaad hai, jo yun likhi ja sakti hai:

blocks.latex: n = \frac{\text{Mass of gas}}{\text{Molar mass of gas}} = \frac{m}{M}
blocks.text_alt: n = gas ka mass / gas ka molar mass = m/M

blocks.text: Is tarah Eq. (6.1) ban jati hai:
Density ρ = m/V hai, is liye:

blocks.text_alt: ρ = m/V,   is liye   ρ = PM/RT   ya   ρ ∝ P/T   (M/R constant hai)

blocks.text: Low pressure aur high temperature par gas ki density kam hoti hai, is liye molecules ek doosre se kaafi door hote hain aur un ke darmiyan forces na hone ke barabar reh jati hain. Is liye real gas low pressure aur high temperature par ideal gas jaisi rehti hai.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text: Real gases ideal gas jaisi ban jati hain: (i) low pressure par (ii) high temperature par.

blocks.text: ρ ∝ P/T ka matlab: pressure kam karein ya temperature barhayein to density kam hoti hai. Density kam = molecules door door = forces kamzor = gas ideal jaisi.

blocks.title: Example 6.1
blocks.problem: Ideal gas ka ek mole 300 K temperature par hai. Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ ho to 1 atm pressure par gas ka volume nikalein. [1 atm = 101325 Pa]
steps: PV = nRT, aur R = Nₐ × k_B (kyun ke k_B = R/Nₐ).
Is liye V = n × Nₐ × k_B × T / P
blocks.answer: Gas ka volume taqreeban 0.025 m³ (yani taqreeban 24.6 litre) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne pressure “1 atom” likha hai; yeh 1 atm hona chahiye. Kitab ka jawab 0.03 m³ hai, magar hisab 0.0246 m³ deta hai, yani taqreeban 0.025 m³. Is liye sahi jawab taqreeban 0.025 m³ hai, 0.03 m³ nahi.
Gas laws (gas ke qawaneen)

Gas ki halat kuch variables (state functions) se bayan hoti hai: pressure, volume aur temperature (P, V aur T). Ek variable badlein aur teesra constant rakhein to doosra variable badalta hai. Ideal gas ke liye in variables ko aapas mein jorne wale qawaneen gas laws kehlate hain.
Boyle's law

Yeh law Robert Boyle ne 1662 mein diya. Yeh constant temperature par gas ke pressure aur volume ka rishta batata hai: ideal gas ke fixed mass ke liye constant temperature par pressure P volume V ke ulta mutabiq (inversely proportional) hai. Volume dugna karein to pressure aadha ho jata hai.
Yani:
Boyle's law ka graph Fig. 6.1 mein hai.

blocks.alt: Dabao P (khari axis) aur volume V (pari axis) ka graph, origin 0. Magenta curve oopar (P1, V1) se tezi se girta hai aur daen taraf (P2, V2) ki taraf chapta hota jata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.1: Boyle ka qanoon graph ki shakal mein (kitab ki Figure 6.1 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Constant temperature par volume V barhta hai to pressure P ghatta hai, is liye curve neeche aata hai. Curve ke har point par P × V ek hi hai: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. Aise curve ko hyperbola kehte hain.
Charles' law

Charles' law constant pressure par ideal gas ke fixed mass ke volume aur temperature ka rishta hai. Yeh French physicist Jacques Charles ne diya. Is ke mutabiq constant pressure par gas ke diye gaye mass ka volume absolute temperature ke seedha mutabiq hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai ke yeh law 1870 mein bana. Yeh durust nahi: Jacques Charles 1823 mein faut ho gaye the; unhon ne yeh law taqreeban 1787 mein maloom kiya aur Gay-Lussac ne 1802 mein chhapa.
Yani:
Is ka graph Fig. 6.2 mein hai.

blocks.alt: Volume V aur temperature T ka graph. Magenta seedhi lakeer daen taraf oopar jati hai; peeche baen taraf barhayein to yeh khari V axis ke baen taraf -273 °C par temperature axis se milti hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.2: Charles ka qanoon graph ki shakal mein (kitab ki Figure 6.2 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Is graph mein temperature °C mein hai. Line ko peeche barhayein to −273 °C par volume zero ho jata hai; yahi absolute zero (0 K) hai. Kelvin mein naapein to line origin se guzarti hai, yani V aur T seedha mutabiq hain.
Gay-Lussac's law
Ideal gas ke fixed mass ke liye constant volume par gas ka pressure us ke absolute temperature ke seedha mutabiq hai.
Yani:
Gay-Lussac's law ka graph Fig. 6.3 mein hai.

blocks.caption: Figure 6.3: Gay-Lussac ka qanoon graph ki shakal mein (kitab ki Figure 6.3 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).
Teen gas laws ek nazar mein

blocks.text: Thermal equilibrium

Jab do cheezein ek hi temperature par hon to dono ki thermal energy (jo particles ki kinetic energy se judi hai) barabar hoti hai. Is liye un ke darmiyan heat ko ek se doosri taraf le jane wali koi wajah (driving force) nahi rehti, aur woh thermal equilibrium (garmi ka tawazun, yani barabari) mein rehti hain.
Misal
Jab hum dhaat (metal) ka chamach garam coffee ke cup mein dalte hain:

items: shuru mein coffee chamach se zyada garam hoti hai,
waqt ke saath heat coffee se chamach mein jati hai,
aakhir coffee aur chamach ka temperature ek jaisa ho jata hai.

blocks.text: Is point par thermal equilibrium ho jata hai: coffee aur chamach ke darmiyan ab koi net heat nahi behti, aur kaha jata hai ke woh thermal equilibrium mein hain.

blocks.prompt: Gas 20 °C par 400 mL jagah leti hai. Constant pressure par 80 °C par us ka volume kitna hoga?
blocks.explanation: Charles' law: V₂ = V₁ × T₂/T₁. Temperature Kelvin mein lein: T₁ = 20 + 273 = 293 K, T₂ = 80 + 273 = 353 K. V₂ = 400 mL × 353/293 ≈ 482 mL.

blocks.prompt: Ek gas 2 atm aur 300 K par hai. Constant volume par 450 K par us ka pressure kitna hoga?
blocks.explanation: Gay-Lussac's law: P₂ = P₁ × T₂/T₁ = 2 atm × 450/300 = 3 atm.

blocks.prompt: Real gas kin halaat mein ideal gas jaisi rehti hai, aur kyun?
blocks.explanation: Low pressure aur high temperature par. ρ ∝ P/T hai, to in halaat mein density kam hoti hai, molecules ek doosre se door hote hain aur un ke darmiyan forces na hone ke barabar reh jati hain; yahi ideal gas ki shart hai.

blocks.text: Mukhtasar khulasa

items: Kinetic theory: random harkat, apna volume negligible, koi intermolecular force nahi, elastic takkarein, bohat se particles, ausat K.E. ∝ absolute T, pressure takkaron se, takkar ka waqt negligible. Real gases high pressure aur low temperature par in se hat jati hain.
Ideal gas: PV = nRT (R = 8.3145 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹); ρ = PM/RT, ρ ∝ P/T; PV = N k_B T, k_B = R/Nₐ = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.
Boyle: PV = constant (T constant); Charles: V/T = constant (P constant); Gay-Lussac: P/T = constant (V constant). Thermal equilibrium: ek hi temperature, koi net heat flow nahi.
